senses.gloss: atha, followed by khalu, tarhi, or evaṃ (= Pali atha, and atha kho; seems not used in this sense in Skt.), after a negative clause: atha khalu (not …) but rather, Ger. sondern Mv 〔ii.161.15, 18〕; 〔162.1, 3〕; atha tarhi, id., LV 〔19.11, 16, 20〕; 〔20.3〕; atha evaṃ anyatra Mv 〔iii.66.8〕 and 15 (see s.v. anyatra, 1), but rather, on the contrary …

atharvaṇa, nt., Atharvanic practices, sorcery, black magic: Divy 〔629.16〕 (mss.; ed. em. āth˚). Pali (Sn 〔927〕) has v.l. athabbaṇa for edd. āth˚; Skt. has atharvaṇa also but apparently not in precisely this sense.
atharvaṇika, a member of a school of the AV: Divy 〔633.10 ff.〕
